touches.text: Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so direct lines to trouble make sense for recovery reasons (7.3.4).
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).

The intention for a trouble ticket is that it is a diagnostic report. EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
In the event a second trouble is observed while the first is open, a new ticket is NEVER issued, we just increment a counter on the ticket.

A trouble has a point of origin, and that is how we match them up. When raised with a condition, its emission source AND error message are checked against open tickets. If found, increment the counter; either way, pass the ticket back to the caller.
The incrementing is part of the trouble ticket class.
So the error a raiser reports is the same words every time it happens; whatever changes from one time to the next (a pid, a timestamp, a temp path) goes in the details, not the error.
Trouble tickets (3.3.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.2.8.1.3).

conflicts.text: The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.
conflicts.ticket_says: Every component raises a trouble for any unfillable request mechanically; later a seam will filter out classes like CLI typos that shouldn't be troubles.
conflicts.why: The outline prescribes: 'The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble.' The outline evaluates *before* raising; the ticket raises *then* evaluates. These produce opposite outcomes: the outline excludes CLI typos from troubles; the ticket includes them (initially). Both cannot coexist.

open_questions.text: Claude Code itself calls Anthropic directly, around the proxy. Is that "an error" to fix someday (CC's calls routed through it), or is CC outside the rule as an external device?
